promptText: Everyone should be allowed to study at university, no matter what their high school grades are. Do you agree or disagree?

phases.correct: Letting students of all skill levels go to university.
distractors: The rising cost of tuition fees for students at public universities.
The choice between academic degrees and practical job training after school.
The number of university graduates that the job market can actually hire.

phases.correct: The need to keep high standards on the hardest university degree courses.
distractors: The need to save every university place for the absolute best students in the country.
The pressure on universities to publish more academic research than they did before.
The competition between countries to attract wealthy fee-paying students from abroad.

phases.correct: making sure difficult university courses are taken by students who can handle the hard work
distractors: making sure that university places only go to students with the highest school exam grades
charging much higher fees so that only the most serious students apply for a university place
limiting the total number of places so that every university class size stays comfortably small

phases.correct: Strict entry rules set by the top research universities.
distractors: Entrance interviews used by elite schools to select the smartest pupils at the age of eleven.
Medical and engineering degrees that require very high grades in mathematics before joining.
Special scholarships offered to a small number of outstanding students every single year.

phases.correct: strict entry rules keep society unequal, because school grades often depend on a family's wealth
distractors: school exam results never truly show what a young person is actually capable of achieving
some highly intelligent students prefer to start working rather than continue studying
top universities spend much more money on research than they spend on teaching students

phases.correct: Removing the money and background barriers that stop people from studying.
distractors: Ending all tuition fees so that no student ever has to borrow money in order to study.
The right of every adult to return to school or college at any point during their life.
The duty of all universities to accept more students from poor countries around the world.

phases.correct: helping people from poorer families go to university and improve their chances in life
distractors: giving every single person who applies a place, whether they can do the hard work or not
offering evening and part-time classes so that people who already have jobs can study
reducing the number of years it takes to get a degree so students start working sooner

phases.correct: The success of open-entry local colleges in towns across North America.
distractors: The success of free online courses that anyone in the world can join from their home.
The growth of apprenticeships that mix paid on-the-job training with part-time college study.
The rise in the number of older students who return to college many years after leaving school.

phases.correct: letting everyone into university can lower teaching standards and cost too much money
distractors: no university anywhere has ever taught a very large class as well as a small group
students from poorer families often have to work long hours alongside their university studies
many young people choose to study a subject that does not really suit their skills at all

phases.correct: entry should be open for basic college courses, but strict for advanced university degrees
distractors: entry should be open to everyone because education is a basic right rather than a prize to win
governments should expand practical training colleges instead of sending more people to university
universities themselves should decide who to accept without any government rules getting in the way

phases.correct: a fair system must give everyone a chance to learn while keeping standards high for top research
distractors: wider access to education is always more valuable than protecting strict academic standards
young people should be completely free to choose whichever university course interests them
a country needs both a smart workforce and top universities that can compete with the best abroad
